rapport_notes: Extremely accommodating — rearranged the arrival window to protect the customer's sleeping daughter without being asked twice, and stayed warm and reassuring throughout.

evidence_quotes.agenda: 'Before I kind of get started here, did you have any just questions or concerns that I can address just write out the gate for you.' — asked immediately, before any address/item questions.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised the 'literally next door' logistics point; rep dug in over several turns ('So once like if we come out the front door, or is it down the street...', 'what is the access look like...is it a driveway?') rather than a single question and pivot.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'if it only takes them an hour to move those things... if there's some other things that they can move to get to that two and a half they can do that' (beats-it-pay-less).

top_strength: Led with the agenda question before any probing, then genuinely dug into the unusual 'moving next door' scenario with real follow-up questions to make sure the estimate and logistics actually matched the situation.
coaching_note: No explicit close was made ('the estimate that I'm given to you, I'll go, go right ahead' is vague) — the customer moved to booking on her own initiative. A clear 'would you like me to lock that in?' plus the missing self-prep-tip and window-framing lines would round out Stage 3.
